subject: f:boss:1
evidence: Python's bridge gives the boss its constituent faces; the native document (quiddity-rust/recognition/1) carries only the defining ones (its cylinder). The other face is the plane capping the boss's free end: quiddity-rust finds it, as the boss occurrence's context (bosses::discover at 1bf3db2; checked for every entry), but recognition::document drops the context, so the native feature lacks a face that belongs to it, and its fingerprint's neighbourhood changes with it. Fix: the document carries constituent faces (a quiddity-rust schema change), as for holes.

subject: f:boss:1
evidence: Python's document enrichment restates the boss's height: axial_length and height_above_base are both its height (checked for every boss record in the fixtures). The native document never carries named_dimensions (quiddity-rust src/recognition.rs). draftwright reads them only into the fingerprint's sizes, which therefore differ (fingerprints are counted, not listed: who owns them is open); demand.rs finds the boss's height under `height` either way.

subject: f:hole_pattern:1
evidence: quiddity measures a rectangle's angle from the in-plane basis of the frame its record is in (hole_patterns.rs plane_uv). Python's 90 degrees, in its working frame, and Rust's 0 degrees, in the file's, both put the width along the part's x axis (computed from each frame's basis). draftwright does not read the angle.

subject: f:fillet:3

subject: f:slot_pattern:1
evidence: quiddity's grid angle is measured in the plane basis of its own frame (`_plane_uv`: x -> (y, z), z -> (x, y)). Python's slots cut along its working x (the part's z), so angle 0 puts its columns along its working y, the part's y; quiddity-rust's cut along the part's z, so angle 90 puts its columns along the part's y. The same lattice (rows, cols and both pitches agree); dims/slots.rs reads the angle in the record's frame and finds the same column axis.

subject: rust f:gusset_rib_pattern:1
evidence: The two ribs mirrored about x = 0 (mirror_plane ["x", 0.0]). Python's own recognise_gusset_rib_patterns on this part gives the same GussetRibMirrorPair(mirror_plane=('x', 0.0)) over these ribs (quiddity 0.4.0.dev0, run 2026-10-08), but Python's document publishes no pattern record: enrich_edit_document (_edit_document.py) folds it into its ribs' mirror_sibling dependents, which the bridge drops. So the bridged Analysis has no gusset_rib_pattern and lint/gussets.rs judges the ribs as two lone groups, where draftwright (which reads the result's gusset_rib_patterns, model/detect.py _append_gusset_features) makes one mirrored group with its spacing. The native reading is draftwright's.

subject: f:boss:1
evidence: Python's bridge gives the boss its constituent faces; the native document (quiddity-rust/recognition/1) carries only the defining ones (its cylinder). subject: f:boss:1

subject: f:plate:1
evidence: Python's document enrichment restates the plate's thickness, 50.0: hi - lo of its own record, within its 1e-3 rounding (checked for every plate of every compared recognition). The native document never carries named_dimensions (quiddity-rust src/recognition.rs); draftwright reads them only into the fingerprint's sizes, which therefore differ (fingerprints are counted, not listed: who owns them is open). lint/channels.rs reads the plate's lo and hi, not the named size.

subject: f:polygonal_boss:1
evidence: Python's document enrichment restates the boss's height: axial_length and height_above_base are both top - base (50.0) of its own record (checked for every polygonal boss in the fixtures). The native document never carries named_dimensions (quiddity-rust src/recognition.rs); draftwright reads them only into the fingerprint's sizes, which therefore differ (fingerprints are counted, not listed: who owns them is open). dims/bosses.rs and lint/polygonal.rs read base and top. This boss runs along z, and demand.rs counts a z boss height only when the fingerprint has a height, length or axial_length size: a native polygonal boss's fingerprint has none, so a switch must take its height from top - base or have the document carry it.

subject: f:boss:1
evidence: Python's bridge gives the boss its constituent faces; the native document (quiddity-rust/recognition/1) carries only the defining one (its cylinder). The other face is the boss's own cap at its free end. Constituent faces alone would not mend it: quiddity-rust reads this boss from its other end (its free_end entry), so its context is face 11, the 305 mm plane all four bosses meet, not the cap. Fix: the document carries constituent faces (a quiddity-rust schema change) and the free end is decided by the part, not the frame.

subject: f:boss:1
evidence: Python's bridge gives the boss its constituent faces; the native document (quiddity-rust/recognition/1) carries only the defining ones (its cylinder). The other face is the plane capping the boss's free end: quiddity-rust finds it, as the boss occurrence's context (bosses::discover at 1bf3db2; checked for every entry), but recognition::document drops the context, so the native feature lacks a face that belongs to it, and its fingerprint's neighbourhood changes with it. Fix: the document carries constituent faces (a quiddity-rust schema change), as for holes.

subject: f:boss:1
evidence: Python's document enrichment restates the boss's height: axial_length and height_above_base are both its height (checked for every boss record in the fixtures). The native document never carries named_dimensions (quiddity-rust src/recognition.rs). draftwright reads them only into the fingerprint's sizes, which therefore differ (fingerprints are counted, not listed: who owns them is open); demand.rs finds the boss's height under `height` either way.

subject: f:plate:1
evidence: Python's document enrichment restates the plate's thickness, 50.0: hi - lo of its own record, within its 1e-3 rounding (checked for every plate of every compared recognition). The native document never carries named_dimensions (quiddity-rust src/recognition.rs); draftwright reads them only into the fingerprint's sizes, which therefore differ (fingerprints are counted, not listed: who owns them is open). lint/channels.rs reads the plate's lo and hi, not the named size.

subject: f:polygonal_boss:1
evidence: Python's document enrichment restates the boss's height: axial_length and height_above_base are both top - base (50.0) of its own record (checked for every polygonal boss in the fixtures). The native document never carries named_dimensions (quiddity-rust src/recognition.rs); draftwright reads them only into the fingerprint's sizes, which therefore differ (fingerprints are counted, not listed: who owns them is open). dims/bosses.rs and lint/polygonal.rs read base and top. This boss runs along z, and demand.rs counts a z boss height only when the fingerprint has a height, length or axial_length size: a native polygonal boss's fingerprint has none, so a switch must take its height from top - base or have the document carry it.

subject: f:boss:1
evidence: Python's bridge gives the boss its constituent faces; the native document (quiddity-rust/recognition/1) carries only the defining one (its cylinder). The other face is the boss's own cap at its free end. Constituent faces alone would not mend it: quiddity-rust reads this boss from its other end (its free_end entry), so its context is face 11, the 305 mm plane all four bosses meet, not the cap. Fix: the document carries constituent faces (a quiddity-rust schema change) and the free end is decided by the part, not the frame.

subject: f:boss:1
evidence: Python's document enrichment restates the boss's height: axial_length and height_above_base are both its height (checked for every boss record in the fixtures). subject: rust f:plate:1
evidence: A 2.5 mm plate along x on the thumbwheel drive screw, a turned part (Python's recognition has 4 turned steps). Python's standalone recognise_plates gives this same Plate (quiddity 0.4.0.dev0, run 2026-10-08), but Python's orchestrated discovery excludes every solid with a turned step (plates.py `_discover`, `excluded_solids=turned_solids`), so its document has no plate; quiddity-rust's document runs the plates without that exclusion. lint/channels.rs reads plates for a channel's lower wall, so a stray plate can change which wall it finds. Fix: quiddity-rust excludes turned solids from plates as Python's orchestration does.

subject: f:oriented_slot:1
evidence: An OrientedSlot's source passage frame (run sense, u and v) is chosen canonically by the run's dominant component, and its width and long directions by their largest component, in the frame it is recognised in: Python's working frame, mapped here into the part's, and quiddity-rust's caller space, the file's. So the same slot is expressed with other senses and another in-plane basis (quiddity-rust's tests/fixtures/known_framed_document.json (mfcadpp_holdout/467.step, oriented_slots, caller_space, equivalent) shows the same mechanism between quiddity-rust's own default frame and caller space, for the one corpus part with an oriented slot). The origin is a point on the run line: Python's lies at the run's other end (x 7.683) and quiddity-rust's at x 0, and across the run they agree to 0.001 (Python rounds its origin in its working frame, quiddity-rust in the file's). Checked: the slot's prism (its section's four vertices at both ends of its run interval, in the part's coordinates) is the same eight points on both sides to 0.001, the step each side rounds its origin to in its own frame (Python rounds in its working frame, whose origin is (7.683, 16.285, 8.686) and axes (-z, -x, y) in the part's; quiddity-rust in the file's), and its width, length, centre, ends, faces and body key agree. draftwright reads none of these fields (the port draws and lints no oriented slot; its fingerprint takes width and length, which agree).
